text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: CRITICAL - node gpu-worker-17 (us-west1-a) reported unreachable, kernel panic detected by host-monitor
pagerduty: Alert triggered: service=redwood-inference-runtime, escalation_policy=oncall-sre, incident_id=PDINC-4829
jen_k: oncall here, seeing alerts for kubelet NotReady from gpu-worker-17. pulling logs now
mike_infra: acked. i'm nearby, can jump in if needed
liz_sre: adding context: we've seen burst of PodEvicted and OOM logs on that host earlier today
sahil_prod: customer-facing spike: some hosted API requests to model xg-8 report 500s and latency ~2-3s higher. possible placement issues
jen_k: running quick check:
```
kubectl get nodes | grep NotReady
# gpu-worker-17   NotReady  120m   v1.26.3  ip-10-0-17-45  us-west1-a
kubectl describe node gpu-worker-17 | egrep -A3 "Kernel" 
# Kernel panic: nop 0x0 at ... stack trace
```
jen_k: can we cordon/drain and move live pods? prefer graceful to avoid disruptions
mike_infra: cordoning now
mike_infra: `kubectl cordon gpu-worker-17` -> success
mike_infra: starting drain: `kubectl drain gpu-worker-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (some GPU pods stuck but controller will recreate elsewhere)
jen_k: creating temporary placement override to favor other AZs while we remediate
liz_sre: checking node exporter metrics — we saw sudden drop in host heartbeat at 21:12 UTC
tia_ops: paging infra on-call in cloud: @cloudops we've got a kernel panic on gpu-worker-17, possible underlying host hardware issue
cloudops-bot: CloudOps incident created: COPS-789, host instance id i-0f3b... in us-west1-a marked unreachable
sahil_prod: status: approx 4% of traffic impacted (mostly long-tail heavy generation flows). telling CS to prepare note
jen_k: mitigation steps so far: cordon+drain, forced pod move for stalled gpus, re-route new inference requests away from region us-west1-a via routing policy
mike_infra: tried SSH to host -> no response, pings time out
mike_infra: trying cloud provider soft-reboot via console (non-forced)
cloudops-bot: soft-reboot initiated for i-0f3b..., status=initiated
jen_k: if reboot doesn't come up, we'll evict node from autoscaling group and replace
liz_sre: checking kubelet logs from last known heartbeat (pulled from journald via central logging):
```
<kernel>: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000000
<kernel>: CPU: 1 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/1 Not tainted 5.15.0
<kubelet>: nodeAuthorizer: node has final taint
```
tia_ops: rolling replacement plan: provision new node in same pool with fresh image + nvidia-driver, then cordon old and remove from pool
jen_k: i'm going to start postmortem tracking doc and timeline. linking runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-node-failure
sahil_prod: opened support ticket for customers impacted, referencing PDINC-4829 and COPS-789
mike_infra: soft-reboot failed, console shows host unreachable. escalating to hardware team
mike_infra: hardware team recommends force-terminate -> recreate (possible host-level kernel panic persistent)
hardware-bot: hardware ticket HW-3421 created, owner @alex_hw
jen_k: brief customer message drafted: "We're investigating an issue affecting a small subset of inference requests in us-west1-a. We're rerouting traffic and provisioning replacement hosts; we'll update shortly." Will post after mike confirms.
liz_sre: while replacement comes up, we need to ensure KV caches warm on new hosts to avoid latency spikes; enabling cache-warm strategy for model xg-8
mike_infra: terminating instance i-0f3b... now (force)
cloudops-bot: Termination initiated. New instance launching by autoscaler in pool gpu-pool-usw1
mike_infra: new node gpu-worker-24 coming up, kubelet joined at 21:27 UTC
jen_k: new node ready, uncordon and let controllers schedule GPU pods back
mike_infra: `kubectl uncordon gpu-worker-24` -> success. pods are re-creating. monitoring
sahil_prod: observed error rate for model xg-8 dropping back to baseline after reroute + replacement
tia_ops: preparing oncall handoff: i'm taking next 8h after 21:45 UTC. cap to check: kernel panic root cause investigation and host replacement completion
jen_k: handing off to @mike_infra for follow-up on hardware ticket and verification of cluster stability. notes: PDINC-4829, COPS-789, HW-3421
mike_infra: ack handoff. will validate logs, ensure no other hosts showing similar traces, and follow up with hardware for RCA
liz_sre: leaving a short checklist for handoff:
- ensure no NotReady nodes
- validate GPU driver versions on new hosts
- check model latency SLOs for next 2 hours
- collect dmesg/kern logs from failed host if hardware can mount disk
jen_k: adding timeline to postmortem doc: initial panic detected 21:12 UTC, cordon+drain 21:14-21:18, soft-reboot fail 21:20, force-terminate 21:24, replacement join 21:27, user impact mitigated 21:30
jen_k: tagging SRE and Infra leads; will convert to incident ticket (INC-2026) for full postmortem
mike_infra: quick sanity checks done. no other nodes with the same kernel oops signature. continuing hardware follow-up
sahil_prod: customer comms sent to affected customers. CS confirms no escalations at this time
tia_ops: handing off to night oncall @liz_sre at 21:45 UTC. leaving contact for HW owner @alex_hw
liz_sre: acknowledged handoff. will run through checklist and validate stable for 2h
jen_k: great. closing active pager for oncall - please update incident timeline when RCA available :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident PDINC-4829 acknowledged by jen_k; status=acknowledged
pagerduty: Incident PDINC-4829 transitioned to resolved (condition: service health restored) - closed by jen_k at 21:35 UTC with note: replacement node and reroute mitigated impact
mike_infra: final note: saved kernel panic snippet and attached to HW-3421 for hardware team's debug. will follow up on firmware/drivers mismatch hypothesis
liz_sre: added postmortem outline to drive, assigned action items
jen_k: thanks everyone. I'll draft the blameless postmortem and link to this thread"
